minutes.headline: Screening committee approved the town manager position profile and set interview dates for December 11 and 12.
minutes.summary: The consultant presented the town manager position statement, built from interviews with select board members and department heads. Members discussed wording (soft skills, "diffuse conflict", "bedroom community", economic development) and agreed to small edits, then a motion to approve the profile was made and seconded. The rest of the meeting set the schedule for candidate selection and interviews, which will be held in executive session.

what_happened.line: The Town Manager Screening Committee approved the town manager position profile by voice vote, with small wording edits and no opposition heard.
Interviews with candidates were set for December 11 and 12 at 6 pm at an off-site location, with the consultant to email about booking.
The meeting to choose which candidates to interview was set for Monday, November 18, at 7, in executive session.
Candidate discussions will be confidential: minutes will refer to candidates by number and only finalists will be named publicly.
The return date originally set for October 31 moved to November 8, and candidates will be asked to bring a document they authored and speak to it.

why_it_matters: The profile sets the criteria the committee will use to screen candidates for town manager, so residents who want a say in what the job requires have the least time to give it before interviews begin.
Because candidate discussions are confidential and minutes use numbers, the public will see names only at the finalist stage, so that is the point at which public input becomes possible.
